verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              युधिष्ठिरस्य नृपतेर्दुर्योधनपितुस्तदा। नान्तरं ददृशू राज्ये पुरुषाः प्रणयं प्रति॥१॥
verses.english: The people who lived in the Kuru kingdom could not mark any difference in the cordiality which existed between king Yudhishthira and the father of Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: यदा तु कौरवो राजा पुत्रं सस्मार दुर्मतिम्। तदा भीमं हृदा राजन्नपध्याति स पार्थिवः॥२॥
verses.english: When the Kuru king recollected his wicked son, he then could not but feel unfriendly, in his heart, towards Bhima.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्। नामर्षयत राजेन्द्र सदैव दुष्टवद्धृदा॥३॥
अप्रकाशान्यप्रियाणि चकारास्य वृकोदरः। आज्ञां प्रत्यहरच्चापि कृतज्ञैः पुरुषैः सदा॥४॥
verses.english: Vrikodara secretly did many deeds that were disagreeable to the old king. Through deceitful servants he caused the commands of his uncle to be disobeyed.

verses.sanskrit: स्मरन्दुर्मन्त्रितं तस्य वृत्तान्यप्यस्य कानिचित्। अथ भीमः सुहृन्मध्ये बाहुशब्दं तथाकरोत्॥५॥
verses.english: Recollecting the evil advice of the old king and some deeds of his, Bhima, one days, in the midst of his friends, slapped his armpits, in the hearing of Dhritarashtra and of Gandhari. The angry Vrikodara, recollecting his enemies Duyrodhana and Karna and Dushasana, gave way to a fit of passion, and said these harsh words :-'The sons of the blind king, capable of fighting with various kinds of weapons, have all been dispatched by me to the other world with these arms of mine which resemble a pair of iron clubs.

verses.sanskrit: संश्रवे धृतराष्ट्रस्य गान्धार्याश्चाप्यमर्षणः। स्मृत्वा दुर्योधनं शत्रुं कर्णदुःशासनावपि॥६॥
प्रोवाचेदं सुसंरब्धो भीमः स परुषं वचः। अन्धस्य नृपतेः पुत्रा मया परिघबाहुना॥७॥
नीता लोकममुं सर्वे नानाशस्त्रास्त्रयोधिनः। इमौ तौ परिघप्रख्यौ भुजौ मम दुरासदौ॥८॥
verses.english: Indeed, these are those two arms of mine, loO king like maces of iron, and invincible by cnemies, coming within whose clasp the sons of Dhritarashtra have all been killed.

verses.sanskrit: ययोरन्तरमासाद्य धार्तराष्ट्राः क्षयं गताः। ताविमौ चन्दनेनाक्तौ चन्दनार्हौ च मे भुजौ॥९॥
verses.english: These are those two well-developed and round arms of mine, resembling a pair of elephantine trunks. Coming within their clasp, the foolish sons of Dhritarashtra have all been killed.

verses.sanskrit: याभ्यां दुर्योधनो नीतः क्षयं ससुतबान्धवः। एताश्चान्याश्च विविधाः शल्यभूता नराधिपः॥१०॥
verses.english: Smeared with sandal-paste and deserving of that adornment are those two arms of mine by which Duryodhana has been sent to the other world along with all his sons and kinsmen.'

verses.sanskrit: वृकोदरस्य ता वाचः श्रुत्वा निर्वेदमागमत्। सा च बुद्धिमती देवी कालपर्यायवेदिनी॥११॥
verses.english: Hearing these and many other words, O king, of Vrikodara, which were so many darts, king Dhritarashtra gave way to cheerlessness and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारी सर्वधर्मज्ञा तान्यलीकानि शुश्रुवे। ततः पञ्चदशे वर्षे समतीते नराधिपः॥१२॥
verses.english: Queen Gandhari, however, who conversant with every duty and endued with great intelligence, and who knew what Time brings on its course, considered them as untrue.

verses.sanskrit: राजा निर्वेदमापेदे भीमवाग्बाणपीडितः। नान्वबुध्यत तद्राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥१३॥
verses.english: Then, after fifteen years had passed away, o monarch, king Dhritarashtra, afflicted (constantly) by the wordy arrows of Bhima, became stricken with despair and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: श्वेताश्वो वाथ कुन्ती वा द्रौपदी वा यशस्विनी। माद्रीपुत्रौ च धर्मज्ञौ चित्तं तस्यान्ववर्तताम्॥१४॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira thc son of Kunti, however, knew it not; nor Arjuna of white horses; nor Kunti; nor Draupadi possessed of great fame; nor the twin sons of Madri, knowing every duty and who were always engaged in acting after the wishes of Dhritarashtra. was to

verses.sanskrit: राज्ञस्तु चित्तं रक्षन्तौ नोचतुः किञ्चिदप्रियम्। ततः स मानयामास धृतराष्ट्रः सुहृज्जनम्॥१५॥
verses.english: Employed in doing the behest's of the king, the twins never said anything that was disagreeable the old king. Then Dhritarashtra one day honoured his friends by his confidence. Addressing them with tearful eyes, he said these words.

verses.sanskrit:
बाष्पसन्दिग्धमत्यर्थमिदमाह च तान्भृशम्।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              विदितं भवतामेतद्यथा वृत्तः कुरुक्षयः॥१६॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said You know how the destruction of Kurus has happened. All that was brought about by my fault, though the Kauravas approved of all my counsels.

verses.sanskrit: ममापराधात्तत्सर्वमनुज्ञातं च कौरवैः। योऽहं दुष्टमतिं मन्दो ज्ञातीनां भयवर्धनम्॥१७॥
verses.english: Fool that I was, I installed the wickedminded Duryodhana, that enhancer of the terrors of kinsmen, to rule over the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनं कौरवाणामाधिपत्यऽभ्यषेचयम्। यच्चाहं वासुदेवस्य नाश्रौषं वाक्यमर्थवत्॥१८॥
वध्यतां साध्वयं पापः सामात्य इति दुर्मतिः। पुत्रस्नेहाभिभूतस्तु हितमुक्तो मनीषिभिः॥१९॥
verses.english: Vasudeva had said to me, 'Let this sinful wretch of wicked understanding be slain along with all his friends and counselors.' I did not listen to those words of great significance. All wise men gave me the same beneficial advice. Vidura, Bhishina, Drona, and Kripa said the same thing. The holy and great Vyasa repeatedly said the same, as also Sanjaya and Gandhari. Overwhelmed, however, by filial affection, I could not follow that advice. Bitter repentance is now my lot for my neglect.

verses.sanskrit: विदुरेणाथ भीष्मेण द्रोणेन च कृपेण च। पदे पदे भगवता व्यासेन च महात्मना॥२०॥
सञ्जयेनाथ गान्धार्या तदिदं तप्यते च माम्। यच्चाहं पाण्डुपुत्रेषु गुणवत्सु महात्मसु॥२१॥
न दत्तवान् श्रियं दीप्तां पितृपैतामहीमिमाम्। विनाशं पश्यमानो हि सर्वराज्ञां गदाग्रजः॥२२॥
verses.english: I also repent for not having bestowed that blazing prosperity, derived from sires and grandsires on the great Pandavas possessed of every accomplishment.

verses.sanskrit: एतच्छ्रेयस्तु परमममन्यत जनार्दनः। सोऽहमेतान्यलीकानि निवृत्तान्यान्मनस्तदा॥२३॥
verses.english: The eldest brother of Gada foresaw the destruction of all the king; Janardana, however, considered that destruction as highly beneficial.

verses.sanskrit: हृदये शल्यभूतानि धारयामि सहस्रशः। विशेषतस्तु पश्यामि वर्षे पञ्चदरोऽद्य वै॥२४॥
verses.english: So many battalions of troops belonging to me, have been destroyed! Alas, my heart is pierced with thousands of darts on account of all these results.

verses.sanskrit: अस्य पापस्य शुद्ध्यर्थं नियतोऽस्मि सुदुर्मतिः। चतुर्थे नियते काले कदाचिदपि चाष्टमे॥२५॥
verses.english: Of wicked understanding as I am, now, after the lapse of fifteen years, I am trying to expiate my sins.

verses.sanskrit: तृष्णाविनयनं भुञ्जे गान्धारी वेद तन्मम। करोत्याहारमिति मां सर्वः परिजनः सदा॥२६॥
verses.english: Now at the fourth division of the day or sometimes at the eighth division, with the regularity of a vow, I eat a little food for simply satisfying my thirst. Gandhari knows this.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरभयादेति भृशं तप्यति पाण्डवः। भूमौ शये जप्यपरो दर्भेष्वजिनसंवृतः॥२७॥
verses.english: All my attendants believe that I eat as usual. Through feat of Yudhishthira alone I concealed my deeds, for if the eldest son of Pandu came to know of my vow, he would feel great pain.
verses.bhavadeepa: तृष्णाविनयनं तृषामात्रापहं मण्डादि न तु क्षुद्व्याधिहरम्॥२६॥

verses.sanskrit: नियमव्यपदेशेन गान्धारी च यशस्विनी। हतं शतं तु पुत्राणां ययोर्युद्धेऽपलायिनाम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Clad in deer-skin, I lie down on the Earth, spreading a small quantity of Kusha grass, and pass the time in silent recitations. The illustrious Gandhari, also, passes her time in the observance of similar vows.

verses.sanskrit: नानुतप्यामि तच्चाहं क्षत्रधर्मं हि ते विदुः। इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजानमभ्यभाषत कौरवः॥२९॥
भद्रं ते यादवीमातर्वचश्चेदं निबोध मे। सुखमसम्युषितः पुत्र त्वया सुपरिपालितः॥३०॥
महादानानि दत्तानि श्राद्धानि च पुनः पुनः। प्रकृष्टं च यया पुत्र पुण्यं चीर्णं यथाबलम्॥३१॥
verses.english: Cherished by you, O son, I have lived these years very happily. I have (with your help) made large gifts and performed Sharaddhas repeatedly.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारी हतपुत्रेयं धैर्येणोदीक्षते च माम्। द्रौपद्या ह्यपकर्तारस्तव चैश्वर्यहारिणः॥३२॥
verses.english: I have, O son, to the best of my power, acquired merit largely. This Gandhari, though destitute of sons, has lived with great fortitude, loO king all the while at me.

verses.sanskrit: समतीता नृशंसास्ते स्वधर्मेण हता युधि। न तेषु प्रतिकर्तव्यं पश्यामि कुरुनन्दन॥३३॥
verses.english: They who inflicted great wrongs on Draupadi and robbed you of your affluence, those cruel men-have all left the world, killed in battle according to the practice of their order.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे शस्त्रभृतां लोकान् गतास्तेऽभिमुखं हताः। आत्मनस्तु हितं पुण्यं प्रतिकर्तव्यमद्य वै॥३४॥
verses.english: I have nothing to do for them, O delighter of the Kurus! Killed with their faces towards battle, they have attained to those regions which reserved for the wielders of weapons.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्याश्चैव राजेन्द्र तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि। त्वं तु शस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठः सततं धर्मवत्सलः॥३५॥
verses.english: I should now, do what is bencficial and meritorious for me as also for Gandhari. O great king, you should grant mc permission. are

verses.sanskrit: राजा गुरुः प्राणभृतां तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया वीर संश्रयेयं वनान्यहम्॥३६॥
verses.english: You are the foremost of all righteous persons. You are always devoted to virtue. The king is the preceptor of all creatures. It is for this that I say so.

verses.sanskrit: चीरवल्कलभृद्राजन् गान्धार्या सहितोऽनया। तवाशिषः प्रयुञ्जानो भविष्यामि वनेचरः॥३७॥
verses.english: With your permission, O hero, I shall retire into the forest, clad in rags and darks, O king, along with this Gandhari.

verses.sanskrit: उचितं नः कुले तात सर्वेषां भरतर्षभ। पुत्रेष्वैश्वर्यमाधाय वयसोऽन्ते वनं नृप॥३८॥
verses.english: I shall live in the forest, always blessing you. It is proper, O son, for the members of our family, to make over sovereignty, when old age comes, to children and lead the forest mode of life. Living there on air alone, or abstaining froin all food, I shall, with this wife of mine, O hero, practice severe austeities.

verses.sanskrit: तत्राहं वायुभक्षो वा निराहारोऽपि वा वसन्। पत्न्या सहानया वीर चरिष्यामि तपः परम्॥३९॥
त्वं चापि फलभाक्तात तपसः पार्थिवो ह्यसि। फलभाजो हि राजानः कल्याणस्येतरस्य वा॥४०॥
verses.english: You shall be a sharer of those penances, o son, for you are the king. Kings are sharers of both auspicious and inauspicious acts done in their kingdom.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              न मां प्रीणयते राज्यं त्वय्येवं दुःखिते नृप। धिङ्नामस्तु सुदुर्बुद्धिं राज्यसक्तं प्रमादिनम्॥४१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said When you, O king, are thus subject to grief, sovereignty does not please me at all. Fie on me who am of wicked understanding, devoted o the pleasures of own and absolutely negligent of my true concerns.

verses.sanskrit: योऽहं भवन्तं दुःखार्तमुपवासकृशं भृशम्। जिताहारं क्षितिशयं न विन्दे भ्रातृभिः सह॥४२॥
verses.english: Alas, I, with all my brothers, was ignorant of yourself having so long been stricken with grief, emaciated with fasts, abstaining from food, and lying on the naked earth.

verses.sanskrit: अहोऽस्मि वञ्चितो मूढो भवता गूढबुद्धिना। विश्वासयित्वा पूर्वं मां यदिदं दुःखमश्नुथाः॥४३॥
verses.english: Alas, foolish that I am, I have been deceived by you who have great intelligence, inasmuch as, having filled me with confidence at first you have latterly undergone such grief.

verses.sanskrit: किं मे राज्येन भोगैर्वा किं यज्ञैः किं सुखेन वा। यस्य मे त्वं महीपाल दुःखान्येतान्यवाप्तवान्॥४४॥
verses.english: What need have I of kingdom or of articles of enjoyment, what need of sacrifices or of happiness, when you, O king, have undergone so much affliction.

verses.sanskrit: पीडितं चापि जानामि राज्यमान्मानमेव च। अनेन वचसा तुभ्यं दुःखितस्य जनेश्वर॥४५॥
verses.english: I consider my kingdom as a disease, and myself also as afflicted. Plunged though I am in sorrow, what however, is the sue of these words that I am addressing you?

verses.sanskrit: भवान्पिता भवान्माता भवान्नः परमो गुरुः। भवता विप्रहीणा वै क्व नु तिष्ठामहे वयम्॥४६॥
verses.english: You are our father, you are our mother; you are our foremost of superiors. Deprived of your presence, how shall we live.

verses.sanskrit: औरसो भवतः पुत्रो युयुत्सुर्नृपसत्तम। अस्तु राजा महाराज यमन्यं मन्यते भवान्॥४७॥
अहं वनं गमिष्यामि भवान् राज्यं प्रशासतु। न मामयशसा दग्धं भूयस्त्वं दग्धुमर्हसि॥४८॥
verses.english: I shall go into the forest. Do you rule the kingdom You should not burn me who am already burned by infamy.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं राजा भवान् राजा भवतः परवानहम्। कथं गुरुं त्वां धर्मज्ञमनुज्ञातुमिहोत्सहे॥४९॥
verses.english: I am not the king. You are the king. I am dependent on your will. How can I dare grant permission to you who are my preceptor?

verses.sanskrit: न मन्युर्हदि नः कश्चित्सुयोधनकृतेऽनघ। भवितव्यं तथा तद्धि वयं चान्ये च मोहिताः॥५०॥
verses.english: O sinless one, I cherish no resentment in my heart on account of the wrongs done to us by Suyodhana. It was ordained that it should be so. Both ourselves and others were stupefied (by fate).

verses.sanskrit: वयं पुत्रा हि भवतो यथा दुर्योधनादयः। गान्धारी चैव कुन्ती च निर्विशेषे मते मम॥५१॥
verses.english: We are your children as Duryodhana and others were. My conviction is that Gandhari is as much my mother as Kunti.

verses.sanskrit: स मां त्वं यदि राजेन्द्र परित्यज्य गमिष्यसि। पृष्ठतस्त्वनुयास्यामि सत्यमात्मानमालभे॥५२॥
verses.english: If you, O king of kings, go to the forest leaving me, I shall then follow you. I swear by iny soul.

verses.sanskrit: इयं हि वसुसम्पूर्णा मही सागरमेखला। भवता विप्रहीणस्य न मे प्रीतिकरी भवेत्॥५३॥
verses.english: This Earth, with her belt of seas, so full of riches, will not be a source of joy to me when I am deprived of your presence.

verses.sanskrit: भवदीयमिदं सर्वं शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये। त्वदधीनाः स्म राजेन्द्र व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥५४॥
verses.english: All this belongs to you. Bending my head low I make my obeisance. We are all dependent on you, O king of kings. Let the fever of your heart be removed.

verses.sanskrit: भवितव्यमनुप्राप्तो मन्ये त्वं वसुधाधिप। दिष्ट्या शुश्रूषमाणस्त्वां मोक्षिष्ये मनसो ज्वरम्॥५५॥
verses.english: I think, O king, that all this that has come upon you is due to destiny. By good luck, I had thought, that waiting upon you and executing your commands obediently, I would rescue you from the fever of your heart.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तापस्ये मे मनस्तात वर्तते कुरुनन्दन। उचितं च कुलेऽस्माकमरण्यगमनं प्रभो॥५६॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said-Odelighter of the Kurus, my mind is fixed, O son, on penances. O powerful one, it is proper for our family that I should retire into the forest.

verses.sanskrit: चिरमस्म्युषितः पुत्र चिरं शुश्रूषितस्त्वया। वृद्धं मामप्यनुज्ञातुमर्हसि त्वं नराधिप॥५७॥
verses.english: I have lived long under your protection, O son. I have for many years been served by you with respect. I am now old. You should, O king, grant me permission.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              इत्युक्त्वा धर्मराजानं वेपमानं कृताञ्जलिम्। उवाच वचनं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥५८॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having said these words to king Yudhishthira the just, king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, trembling all the while and with hands joined together, further said to the great Sanjaya and the great car-warrior Kripa, these words: I wish to solicit the king through you.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जयं च महात्मानं कृपं चापि महारथम्। अनुनेनुमिहेच्छामि भवद्भिर्वसुधाधिपम्॥५९॥
म्लायते मे मनो हीदं मुखं च परिशुष्यति। वयसा च प्रकृष्टेन वाग्व्यायामेन चैव ह॥६०॥
verses.english: My mind has become dispirited, my mouth has become dry, through the weakness of age and the exertion of speaking.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा स तु धर्मात्मा वृद्धो राजा कुरुद्वहः। गान्धारी शिश्रिये धीमान् सहसैव गतासुवत्॥६१॥
verses.english: Having said so, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., the pious old king, blessed with prosperity, leaned to Gandhari and suddenly looked like one dcad.

verses.sanskrit: तं तु दृष्ट्वा समासीनं विसंज्ञमिव कौरवम्। आर्तिं राजागमत्तीव्रां कौन्तेयः परवीरहा॥६२॥

युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              यस्य नागसहस्रेण शतसङ्ख्येन वै बलम्। सोऽयं नारीं व्यपाश्रित्य शेते राजा गतासुवत्॥६३॥
आयसी प्रतिमा येन भीमसेनस्य सा पुरा। चूर्णीकृता बलवता सोऽबलामाश्रितः स्त्रियम्॥६४॥
verses.english: Alas, he by whom the iron image of Bhima on a former occasion was reduced to pieces, leans today on a weak woman.

verses.sanskrit: धिगस्तु मामधर्मज्ञं धिग्बुद्धिं धिक्च मे श्रुतम्। यत्कृते पृथिवीपालः शेतेऽयमतथोचितः॥६५॥
अहमप्युपवत्स्यामि यथैवायं गुरुर्मम। यदि राजा न भुङ्क्तेऽयं गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥६६॥
verses.english: I also shall fast even as my preceptor. Indeed, I shall fast if this king and Gandhari of great fame abstain from food.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततोऽस्य पाणिना राजन् जलशीतेन पाण्डवः। उरो मुखं च शनकैः पर्यमार्जत धर्मवित्॥६७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said The Pandava king, knowing every duty, using his own hand, then softly rubbed with cold water the breast and the face of the old king.

verses.sanskrit: तेन रत्नौषधिमता पुण्येन च सुगन्धिना। पाणिस्पर्शन राज्ञः स राजा संज्ञामवाप ह॥६८॥
verses.english: At the touch of the king's hand which was auspicious and fragrant, and on which were jewels and medicinal herb's, Dhritarashtra regained his consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              स्पृश मां पाणिना भूयः परिष्वज च पाण्डव। जीवामीवातिसंस्पर्शात्तव राजीवलोचन॥६९॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said Do you, again, touch me, O son of Pandu, with your hand, and do you embrace me. O you having eyes like lotus petals, I am restored to my senses through the auspicious touch of your hand.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्धानं च तवाघ्रातुमिच्छामि मनुजाधिप। पाणिभ्यां हि परिस्प्रष्टुं प्रीणनं हि महन्मम॥७०॥
verses.english: O king, I wish to smell your head. The clasp of your arms is highly gratifying to me.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टमो ह्यद्य कालोऽयमाहारस्य कृतस्य मे। येनाहं कुरुशार्दूल शक्नोमि न विचेष्टितुम्॥७१॥
verses.english: This is the eighth division of the day and therefore, the hour for taking may food. For not having taken my food, O scion of Kuru's race, I am so weak that I cannot move.

verses.sanskrit: व्यायामश्चायमत्यर्थं कृतस्त्वामभियाचता। ततो ग्लानमनास्तात नष्टसंज्ञ इवाभवम्॥७२॥
तवामृतरसप्रख्यं हस्तस्पर्शमिमं प्रभो। लब्धा सञ्जीवितोऽस्मीति मन्ये कुरुकुलोद्वह॥७३॥
verses.english: O perpetuator of Kuru's race, I think that receiving the touch of your hand, which is like nectar in its vivifying effects I have been restored to my senses.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तस्तु कौन्तेयः पित्रा ज्येष्ठेन भारत। पस्पर्श सर्वगात्रेषु सौहार्दात्तं शनैस्तदा॥७४॥
verses.english: Thus addressed, O Bharata, by the eldest brother of his father, the son of Kunti, from affection, gently touched every part of his body.

verses.sanskrit: उपलभ्य ततः प्राणान्धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य मूर्ध्न्याजिघ्रत पाण्डवम्॥७५॥
विदुरादयश्च ते सर्वे रुरुदुर्दुःखिता भृशम्। अतिदुःखात्तु राजानं नोचुः किञ्चन पाण्डवम्॥७६॥
गान्धारी त्वेव धर्मज्ञा मनसोद्वहती भृशम्। दुःखान्यधारयाद्राजन्मैवमित्येव चाब्रवीत्॥७७॥
verses.english: Gandhari, knowing every duty, bore her sorrow with patience, and loaded as her heart was,, O king, said nothing.

verses.sanskrit: इतरास्तु स्त्रियः सर्वाः कुन्त्या सह सुदुःखिताः। नेत्रैरागतविक्लेदैः परिवार्य स्थिताऽभवन्॥७८॥
verses.english: The other ladies, Kunti among them, became greatly afflicted. They wept, shedding profuse tears, and sat surrounding the old king.

verses.sanskrit: अथाब्रवीत्पुनर्वाक्यं धृतराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरम्। अनुजानीहि मां राजस्तापस्ये भरतर्षभ॥७९॥
verses.english: Then Dhritarashtra, once more addressing Yudhishthira, said these words-Do you, O king, permit me to practice penance's.

verses.sanskrit: ग्लायते मे मनस्तात भूयो भूयः प्रजल्पतः। न मामतः परं पुत्र परिक्लेष्टुमिहार्हसि॥८०॥
verses.english: By speaking repeatedly, O son, my mind becomes weakened. You should not, O son, afflict me after this.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तु कौरवेन्द्रे तं तथा ब्रुवति पाण्डवम्। सर्वेषमिव योधानामार्तनादो महानभूत्॥८१॥
दृष्ट्वा कृशं विवर्णं च राजानमतथोचितम्। उपवासपरिश्रान्तं त्वगस्थिपरिवारणम्॥८२॥
verses.english: Seeing his royal father of great splendour, emaciated and palc, reduced to unworthy of him worn out with fasts, and loO king like skeleton covered with skin, Dharma's son Yudhishthira shed tears of grief and once more said these words.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मपुत्रः स्वपितरं परिष्वज्य महाप्रभुम्। शोकजं बाष्पमुत्सृज्य पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत्॥८३॥
न कामये नरश्रेष्ठ जीवितं पृथिवीं तथा। यथा तव प्रियं राजंश्चिकीर्षामि परन्तप॥८४॥
verses.english: When Dhritarashtra said these words to Yudhishthira, Datyavati's son Vyasa came the and said as follows.

verses.sanskrit: इति ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे धृतराष्ट्रे युधिष्ठिरम्। ऋषिः सत्यवतीपुत्रो व्यासोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्॥८४॥
verses.english: When Dhritarashtra said these words to Yudhishthira, Datyavati's son Vyasa came the and said as follows.

verses.sanskrit: यदि चाहमनुग्राह्यो भवतो दयितोऽपि वा। क्रियतां तावदाहारस्ततो वेत्स्याम्यहं परम्॥८५॥
verses.english: If I deserve your favour, if I am dear to you, do you eat something. I shall then know what to do.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया पुत्र भुञ्जीयामिति कामये॥८६॥
